title: Aniimo Alpha Bosses Guide | Every Alpha Location, Weakness And Reward | Aniimo Guide
description: A full guide to the Alpha bosses in Aniimo: where the seventeen Alphas live, early and late fights, element weaknesses, tricks for Turbo, Tubster and Leafy, the Dark Alpha team, first clear rewards and how the free Aniipod catch works. Checked against several guides in October 2026; details can change with patches, so trust your own game.

sections.heading: Meet the Alphas
sections.script: Alpha Aniimo are the big boss creatures of the world, and beating them is one of the best ways to grow your collection. In this video we cover where every Alpha lives, which ones are the easiest to start with, the elements that hurt them most, what you win on your first clear, and how to catch one after the fight. We keep this separate from our catching video and our team building video, because this one is only about the bosses. A friendly warning as usual. Guides do not agree on every number, and patches can change things, so trust what your own game shows you. By the end you will know exactly which Alpha to hunt first and how to prepare.

sections.heading: What is an Alpha
sections.script: An Alpha is a field boss that waits at a fixed spot on the map. Guides list seventeen of them across the world, and each one belongs to a single element. You find them with the Alpha markers on your map. A useful tip is to zoom in, because the markers can disappear when you zoom all the way out. The Institute Guide also shows the rewards for each challenge. Blooms and Sanctums work as fast travel points, so unlock the nearest one before you go. The first Alpha expects a team of around level thirteen, and the later ones scale much higher. So you do not need to rush. Take them one region at a time, and you will always be strong enough for the next.

sections.heading: The early Alphas
sections.script: Let us start with the friendly ones. Alpha Turbo is a Wind boss in Nimbus Fields, northeast of the First Spark Sanctum. Alpha Tubster is another Wind boss, at the Argent Strait, southwest of the same Sanctum. Alpha Stellarys is a Dark boss in the Forest of Falling Stars, north of the Outpost. Alpha Scorchhowl is a Fire boss at Beast Fang Ridge, and guides say Water attackers make that fight much shorter. Alpha Leafy is a Grass boss in the Mistwoods, northeast of the Breezy Plains Branch. All five are great training for how Alpha fights work, so do them first. Each of them also drops a stone or crystal that you can farm again later, which makes these early fights worth repeating when you need materials.

sections.heading: Tricks for Turbo, Tubster and Leafy
sections.script: Each early boss teaches one trick. Alpha Turbo flies, and while it is in the air it is protected, so do not waste your skills. Lure it into the Nimbi, and once two stick to its wool it crashes down and you can break it. Alpha Tubster raises a Storm Shield when it charges, so hit the shield hard to interrupt the attack and leave the boss weakened. Alpha Leafy has a Lotus Essence that you should break when the warning appears, and a healing shield that you should break quickly. The lesson is the same every time. Learn the trick, break the boss, and spend your strongest skills during that window.

sections.heading: The middle Alphas
sections.script: Now the middle of the map. Alpha Glynsera is an Ice boss in an ice cave south of the Sanctum at Beast Fang Ridge, and you need a Fire attacker to melt the ice seal. Alpha Panpanta is a Water boss on the shore at Echoback Landing. Alpha Bouldus is an Earth boss on a hill in Berylline Vale. Alpha Blazen is a Lightning boss on a mountaintop in Blitzwood. Guides say Blazen resists Lightning, so bring Ice and Dark Aniimo instead. Alpha Magmarex is a Fire boss, reached through a geyser at the Zephyrus Landbridge. Bring a healer for this stretch, because the fights get longer. The good news is that every one of these bosses gives you a stone or crystal reward that you can collect again on later runs, so your time is never wasted.

sections.heading: The Dark Alphas
sections.script: Here is a neat shortcut. Alpha Stellarys, Alpha Ignitis and Alpha Rookey are all Dark bosses, and guides say Wind and Light hurt them the most. That means one team can beat all three. Stellarys is in the Forest of Falling Stars. Alpha Ignitis lives in Berylline Vale, southeast of the Bloom, and guides say it appears only at night, so wait for the evening before you go. Alpha Rookey is in the Russet Highlands, east of the First Sight Sanctum, and you should break its guard during the battle. Bring a Wind Aniimo, a Light Aniimo, a Breaker and a healer, and you are ready.

sections.heading: The hidden and late Alphas
sections.script: The last Alphas need a little extra work. Alpha Geoclaw hides in a river cave in Nimbus Fields. To open the way, guides say you must infuse one hundred twenty Lumin Amber into the Breezy Plains Branch. Alpha Minespine waits in the Crystal Cave south of the Forgotten Mine in Beast Fang Ridge. Alpha Grizbo is an Earth boss in Rosetower Woods, and guides say Water and Grass attackers work well. Alpha Irisal is a Grass boss in the Sea of Flowers, and its rotating beams have safe gaps you can step into. Finally Alpha Luminelle is a Lightning boss on the Tideblossom Coast, and guides say it appears after a shooting star lands at night.

sections.heading: Build the right team
sections.script: Preparation wins Alpha fights. Guides suggest a simple team of four roles. First, an Aniimo whose element counters the boss. Second, a Breaker, who fills the break gauge fast. Third, a main damage dealer. Fourth, a healer. Swap out any Aniimo with low health before it faints, and bring healing items, especially if you want to recruit the boss afterwards. Always check the element of the boss before you leave. A wrong element can double the length of the fight, while a right one can end it in a short time. Use the map markers and the Institute Guide to check each boss before you travel, so you never walk in blind. If a fight feels impossible, do not give up. Level your team a little and try again.

sections.heading: Rewards and the Alpha catch
sections.script: Now the rewards. Guides agree that your first clear gives fifty Glimmer, five hundred Safaris experience, an Irisalis Petal and a Lumin Amber from Breezy Plains. Most Alphas also give five element stones, such as the Roar Stone from Blazen. After the fight, the game gives you one free Aniipod for a single catch attempt, and this matters. Throw it, because leaving the catch screen without throwing can forfeit your rewards. Guides say the base catch chance on an Alpha is very low, so use an Aniipod Ultra or a Sparkling Cube if you really want the boss on your team. Collecting rewards also costs thirty Primegy, so keep some in reserve. Primegy slowly refills over time, and guides say you can also restore it with a Primegy Battery, so plan your boss runs around it.

sections.heading: Which Alpha is your favourite
sections.script: That was our full guide to the Alpha bosses in Aniimo. Learn each trick, bring the right element, break the boss and take your free catch. Which Alpha was the hardest for you, and which one did you catch on your very first throw? Tell us in the comments, because we love reading your boss stories.
